cues: Samuel Moyn is an American historian of law, a professor at Yale, known for re-telling the history of human rights with a sceptical eye.
This essay comes from the argument of his book Not Enough.
It is the hardest essay in your book, because it argues instead of telling a story.
But every question comes back to one sentence: human rights are good at stopping state cruelty and guaranteeing a minimum, but they are not equipped to challenge inequality itself.
